title: Swap keys and values
starter:
def invert(d: dict) -> dict:
    return dict(d)
hints: `d.items()` gives each `(key, value)` pair. You want each pair the other way around.
A dict comprehension builds the new dict in one line: `{new_key: new_value for k, v in d.items()}`.
explain: The reference is `{v: k for k, v in d.items()}`. Each pair is unpacked into `k` and `v` and stored the other way around. It assumes the values are all different and hashable. If two keys shared a value, the later one would win.
